respondent:
State Of Maharashtra
Supreme Court of India

5 January 2011
Criminal Appeal No. 14 of 2011 (Arising Out of Slp(Crl.) No. 1981 of 2010)
The Judgment was delivered by : Balbir Singh Chauhan, J.
Leave granted.
1.  This appeal has been preferred against the judgment and order dated 25.8.2009 passed in Criminal Appeal No.242/04 by the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, Nagpur Bench, affirming the judgment and order dated 16.3.2004 passed by 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Nagpur, in Sessions Trial No.366/03 convicting the appellant under Section 302 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter called IPC) and awarding the sentence of life imprisonment and, in addition thereto a fine of Rs.1000/- had also been imposed and in default of payment to undergo further rigorous imprisonment for the period of one year.
2.  Facts and circumstances giving rise to this appeal are that the appellant's sister Sandhya had a love affair with Prashant (deceased) which continued for 2-3 years. The appel
facts: The love affair of Sandhya, sister of the appellant, continued with Prashant (deceased) for 2-3 years.
The appellant did not like the relationship and had altercations with Prashant (deceased) several times.
On seeing both of them together at an odd hour i.e. 9.15 P.M. on 30th April, 2003, he suddenly assaulted Prashant with knife and caused stab injuries.
Later on, Prashant (deceased) succumbed to the said injuries and died on 2nd May, 2003.
issues: The nature of the offence committed by the appellant
petitioner_arguments: As the act of the appellant had not been pre-meditated and it all happened because of sudden provocation, conviction could be only under Section 304, Part I IPC and not under Section 302 IPC.
The fact that the appellant stabbed the deceased twice in the thigh and only once in the chest is indicative of a lack of intention to cause death.
respondent_arguments: Considering the gravity of injuries, no interference is required with the impugned judgment by this Court.
The appellant has rightly been convicted under Section 302 IPC.
court_reasoning: The admitted facts have been that the love affair of Sandhya, sister of the appellant, continued with Prashant (deceased) for 2-3 years.
The fact that the appellant stabbed the deceased twice in the thigh and only once in the chest is indicative of a lack of intention to cause death.

It is not the case even in any of the dying declarations that the appellant had premeditated or pre-planned his actions or was having any information prior to the incident that the deceased would be found with his sister Sandhya at the place of occurrence.
holding: The appeal is disposed of. Appeal disposed of.
The conviction of the appellant from Section 302 IPC to Section 304 Part-I IPC and awarding ten years rigorous imprisonment to the appellant.
